title: Cheap rooms and meals in Omaha and Ottumwa
summary: He tells of a one-dollar room in Omaha with free dinners and a $1.35-a-week Ottumwa room, a sporting house, with one meal a day.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: The Depression years and the WPA band

But you must have been getting more
money. that.
See, I had to pay my room rent out of
Oh, yeah.
That was $1.35 a week.
I don't believe it. Oh, I don't believe that.
That 35 cents was for one meal.
A day?
One meal. I paid a $1.35 a week. And for 35 cents, I'd get one meal a day.
Oh, that's not possible.
That's true.
You were staying in somebody's home, and they fed you?

Once a day.

They got $1.35.

Oh, it was a fairly little town, yes. It was a small town.
I mean, can you I can't believe that.
Well, no, that's what surprised me, because when I left -- before I left Omaha, Nebraska, when I first got there, rather, I had to pay five dollars a week for a room.

And then I met a trumpet player, named Williams. He's in Chicago now. Well, his mother-in-law had a room, and so he told me about this room. And for me to come up and see her about a room. And so I went up there, and he had told me it would be cheaper than five dollars a week. Which was very good, see.
Yeah.
So I asked her, did she have a room, she told me yes. And I went there and saw the room. It was a room with a bed in it, you know, it was clean and everything.
Yeah, yeah.
And so I said, 'How much? I'd like to take the room.' So I said, 'How much would the room be?' So she said, 'Well, since it's you, you can have it for a dollar.'

Isn't that incredible?

And that's the mid-'30s. Of course, it was after Depression. It was still a little bit of Depression, wasn't it?

Yeah.

Isn't that surprising?

Well, you were like a millionaire with your $100 a week.

Yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah.
See what I mean? The madame there, one of those things.

Oh, yes, she -- that was all right, see.
Yeah. Fancy that.
And --
